edges.notes: Bionic is the C library shipped as part of the AOSP core system image and NDK targets.
Android native processes use Bionic as the userspace C library atop the device Linux-based kernel.
Bionic implements C, POSIX subset, and Android-specific APIs for hosted native code on Android.
Android native binaries and shared objects use ELF dynamic linking with the Bionic dynamic linker.
The Android NDK primarily uses Clang/LLVM toolchains that link against Bionic.
NDK C++ stacks commonly use libc++ layered on Bionic for native C++ on Android.
libc++abi pairs with libc++ in typical NDK C++ configurations on Bionic.
Some third-party or legacy native build flows may use GNU binutils components with appropriate Android sysroots.
Legacy or specialized cross-build toolchains may target Bionic with GCC where configured.
